name: io.github.zorcec/vibeflow
title: Vibeflow
description: Kanban task board over MCP for your own repo. Click any element to get a ticket with its selector.

packageArguments.name: mcp
packageArguments.description: Run the MCP server over stdio.

packageArguments.name: --project
packageArguments.description: Project root this server serves. Required, and resolved once at startup: one process serves exactly one repository, so every tool call reads and writes that project's task store. Point it at your own repo.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.longDescription: Vibeflow gives an AI coding agent a Kanban board over the user's own repository: click any element in their app and it becomes a ticket carrying that element's CSS selector, URL, source file and line. Tasks, progress and verification then live in one place instead of being scattered across a chat transcript. It runs locally over stdio, needs no account and no API key, and there is no hosted service to sign up for.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport: stdio, one process per project. An HTTP transport also exists (vibeflow serve, MCP at /api/mcp) but it is a local loopback server, not a public endpoint, so this manifest declares no remotes.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: None. Local-first: no login is required and no API key is needed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.releaseNote: This manifest is pinned to 0.19.2, the published version of @vibeflow-tools/cli. Verified against the published tarball (`npm pack @vibeflow-tools/cli@0.19.2`), not the repository: all 13 tools are present, including `start_kanban` and `get_integration_guide`, which shipped in this release. The `tools` count here therefore matches the README.
